configurations.//: Added Phase 38d-i. Same purpose as refdata-vs-docker (dev server against the dockerized stack) but on 7107, because docker-compose already publishes every port from 7100 to 7106 (nats-ui took 7103, the port refdata-vs-docker's own vite.docker.config.js pins with strictPort) and holds them whenever the stack is up. The base vite.config already proxies /api/auth to accounts-service (7202) and /api to refdata-service (7201), both host ports of the running stack, so no config override is needed here.
configurations.name: refdata-dev-docker-7107

configurations.//: Added Phase 50e. Same collision refdata-dev-docker-7107 documents: docker-compose publishes the built admin image on 7100, so `admin` (autoPort) lets vite bind localhost:7100 alongside it and every request to 127.0.0.1:7100 still reaches the container, not the dev server. --strictPort on a port docker does not hold is the only way to be sure which one you are looking at.
configurations.name: admin-dev-7108

configurations.//: Use admin-dev-7108 above when the docker stack is up. This entry's autoPort resolves the bind collision on 7100 but not the ambiguity it creates: docker-compose publishes the built admin image there, so requests to 127.0.0.1:7100 keep reaching the CONTAINER while vite serves your edits somewhere else. It is only safe with the stack down.
configurations.name: admin

configurations.//: Phase 1a moved the shell off 5170 (this entry said 5176 — it had drifted) into the 7100-7199 frontend range CLAUDE.md defines. 7109 is the first free port: docker-compose publishes 7100-7106 and holds them whenever the stack is up, 7107 and 7108 are claimed above. No autoPort — the point of the move is that the shell is always at a known port, since Phase 1b's example plugin (7110) is loaded by URL.
configurations.name: lab-shell
